gates.name: Windows secure runtime primitives
gates.blocker: Filesystem read isolation for restrictive profiles is still fail-closed and lacks complete native hostile read/write proof.

gates.name: End-to-end Windows product runtime
gates.blocker: Desktop/WinUI exists, exact Release builds and hash-bound Desktop startup/cleanup pass. Mandatory versioned terms acceptance and Desktop -> EngineHost -> worker -> embedded Python -> private Chromium remain implementation/evidence blockers.

gates.name: Installer + lifecycle
gates.blocker: Exact-candidate Windows lifecycle passes interruption recovery, repair after controlled file loss, upgrade, downgrade rejection, uninstall, product-owned residue cleanup and user-data preservation. Mandatory versioned terms acceptance is not yet independently proven on the releasable candidate, so the gate remains PARCIAL. Authenticode is intentionally evaluated separately under distribution-security.

gates.name: Distribution security
gates.blocker: Microsoft Defender scanned both exact installer artifacts successfully with no path-bound detections and unchanged SHA-256 hashes. The AEVRIX installers remain unsigned; Authenticode plus signed update-manifest/tamper/rollback controls remain mandatory before external distribution.

gates.name: Execution Authority + PostgreSQL integration
gates.blocker: The PostgreSQL-backed IExecutionPromotionAuthority adapter is not physically present in the canonical tree; implementation is required before DB-backed AVA can run.

gates.name: Regression + performance + stability
gates.blocker: Authenticated soak plus forced-crash fail-closed recovery and cleanup pass for EngineHost. Full-product Desktop/downstream endurance, recovery and resource behavior remain required.

gates.name: Exact-hash AVA evidence package
gates.blocker: Durable exact-candidate Windows readiness and installer packages exist, but the final AVA package still lacks all mandatory product, signing/update, database, accessibility and full-runtime gates.
